$comment: The shared lens (docs/shared-lens-and-coverage-brief.md §3, §4): cultures, regions, eras, styles and tones defined once; `mappings` says how each module's own rosters read in lens terms. Planned cultures are declared and never offered.

caste.note: Cultures whose names carry caste or trade-guild forms: buildings, events, inns, money, settlement context and streets each kept this pair.

dutchAmerican.note: Money: the cultures whose coin names read the Dutch and American shapes.

britainSource.note: Bynames: cultures that draw their forenames from the British source. Differs from the `british` group: it includes general.

noPlaceNames.note: Peoples and tongues, bynames: cultures with no place-name form.

realmsChristian.note: Realms' own Christian set. Differs from the vocabulary's `christian` group (it includes general and ethiopian): kept as it is.

plainNicknames.note: Named things: cultures whose nickname forms aren't reduced.

routesGods.note: Route names: cultures with god-named routes.

festivalsAncient.note: Time and sky: cultures whose ancient calendars carry festivals.

seasonPairNorth.note: Time and sky: cultures reading a two-season pair from the ancient era to the medieval.

seasonPairMeso.note: Time and sky: cultures reading a season pair from the ancient era to the early modern; also the Mesoamerican calendar round.

elementsEastAsian.note: Time and sky: cultures whose week-7 system reads the five elements.

vesselRealmCultures.note: Vessels: the cultures a realm short form can be drawn for (the realms roster); others read general.

notes.aircraft: Read from docs/aircraft-and-land-vehicles-brief.md §4.1 (the data's `technology` carries labels, not dates): A1 balloons and kites (kites from antiquity, balloons from 1783) AN–ST; A2 airships (1852 to the 1930s) ST, MO; A3 pioneer and biplane (1903 to the 1920s) ST, MO; A4 piston age, A5 jet age and A6 modern and drones MO; A7 future NF, IS; AF sky ships, fantastic only: the eras of the settings that offer it (FH is MD, MF is MO, §4.3).
notes.landVehicles: Read from docs/aircraft-and-land-vehicles-brief.md §4.2: L1 animal-drawn (chariots to coaches, in use throughout) AN–ST; L2 steam ST; L3 early motor (cars from the 1880s, the first tanks, electric trams) ST, MO; L4 mid-century and L5 modern MO; L6 future NF, IS; LF war engines and wonders, fantastic only: MD (FH) and MO (MF).

sourceShares.$comment: Place modules split brief §4.1: where a focused place module's draw comes from, before it falls back to its own shapes. A kind may list sources; the share is the chance a draw tries the source first.
